title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
1. 1. In January 2023 the government, led by Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Women and Special Groups adopted and operationalised a National Multisectoral Generation Equality Program (TGEP) 2022-2026 which considered the priorities for ratification of Convention 190 through sensitization and awareness raising. As a result, a National Advisory Committee consisting of 25 members (19 members from Tanzania mainland and six members from Zanzibar), as well as experts from different sectors was created to oversee the measures geared for achieving gender equality including through promotion for ratification of C.190 and integration of the key principles into national action plans. Sensitization and awareness raising for constituents have therefore been promoted for the ratification of C190 and R206.
2. To ensure the effective implementation of Convention No. 190 and create a world of work free from violence and harassment for all and, in particular, women, in December 2023 the government in consultation with Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE) and Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) adopted a National Action Plan on ending Violence against Women and Children in Tanzania (NPA-VAWC 2023/2024 – 2027/2028). The NPA-VWAC II shapes strategic interventions clustered into different thematic areas including creating safe environment in public and digital spaces and integrated issues of HIV and AIDS as cross-cutting areas as efforts to creating decent work environment for vulnerable workers in the informal sector. The NPA-VAWC II takes into consideration the key principles of the ILO Convention No. 190 and Recommendation No. 206. With support from ILO RBTC funds, the ILO in collaboration with UNWOMEN, Ministry of Community Development, Gender, Women and Special Groups, Association of Tanzania Employers (ATE), Trade Union Congress of Tanzania (TUCTA) and other stakeholders convened a national workshop for awareness raising of ILO C190 which also informed and integrated in the URT Generation Equality Programme (2021/22 – 2025/26) approved and adopted in January 2023.
The ILO provided technical support during drafting of the NPA-VWAC II and facilitated participation of the social partners to make strategic inputs in the document which integrated issues of elimination of sexual harassment and violence at public spaces as one of the strategic thematic area of focus on the NPA-VAWC II. The ILO C.190 and its recommendation were used as references to inform the process.
